turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you start by telling me what's been bringing you in to see me?
turns.patient_response: I'm here because I've started planning my days around not using elevators. It's getting a little ridiculous, to be honest. I'm taking five flights of stairs every day at my apartment now. I even turned down a training workshop recently because it was in a high-rise building and I just couldn't do it. I've also had to stop visiting one of my older computer students because his building doesn't really have a good stair option, and I just can't bring myself to get in the elevator.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient explicitly describes active avoidance of elevators by taking stairs, declining a workshop in a high-rise, and discontinuing visits to a student whose building lacks a good stair option.

turns.doctor_question: When you imagine getting into an elevator, what exactly are you afraid will happen?
turns.patient_response: Well, I know an elevator in a regular office block is probably safe, but... when I look at those old doors in my apartment building, or even the ones at work, my mind just treats it like I'm about to get trapped in there. Or like it's going to drop. Even though part of me knows that sounds a bit over the top, I just can't shake that feeling.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes marked fear of elevators, specifically worrying about being trapped or falling, while recognizing that the reaction is out of proportion to actual safety.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from elevators, do you notice similar intense anxiety in other situations—like crowded places, public transportation, or being far from home—where you feel it might be hard to escape or get help?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. It's pretty much just elevators. I don't have any issues with crowds or taking the bus or anything like that. Being far from home doesn't bother me either. I don't really worry about being trapped anywhere else, it's really only the elevators that make me feel that way.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been experiencing this fear of elevators—when did you first notice it starting?
turns.patient_response: It's been going on for about seven months now. It started shortly after I moved into my current apartment on the fifth floor. There was this one time the elevator kind of jerked and stopped for a minute, and... yeah, that was the scare that set all this off.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient confirms experiencing an ongoing fear of elevators for the past seven months following an incident where an elevator jerked and stopped.
